Antibiotics tested and their zone diameter breakpoints

Source: R/burigangaamr_antibiotics.R
burigangaamr_antibiotics.Rd

The nine antibiotics of the disc diffusion test with their class, disc content and the zone diameter breakpoints used to interpret the results, from supplementary tables S1 and S2.

Usage

burigangaamr_antibiotics

Format

A tibble with 9 rows and 8 variables

antibiotic_code

Short code of the antibiotic disc as used in the supplement: PIT, CTX, CPM, GEN, AK, MRP, IPM, TE or CIP.

antibiotic

Name of the antibiotic.

antibiotic_class

Class of the antibiotic: Penicillins, Cephalosporins, Aminoglycosides, Carbapenems, Tetracyclines or Fluoroquinolones.

disc_content

Amount of antibiotic on the disc used in the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion test, in micrograms, as given in the supplement (100/10 µg for piperacillin-tazobactam).

breakpoint_resistant_max

Largest zone diameter in millimetres that is interpreted as resistant, from supplementary table S2.

breakpoint_intermediate_min

Smallest zone diameter in millimetres that is interpreted as intermediate, from supplementary table S2.

breakpoint_intermediate_max

Largest zone diameter in millimetres that is interpreted as intermediate, from supplementary table S2.

breakpoint_susceptible_min

Smallest zone diameter in millimetres that is interpreted as susceptible, from supplementary table S2.

Source

Sharif, D. I., Amin, F., Mehbub, M. H. and Ratul, R. I. (2024). Distribution and antibiotic resistance patterns of Pseudomonas aeruginosa across different point sources of pollution in the Buriganga River, Bangladesh. Journal of Water and Health, 22(12), supplementary tables S1 and S2. https://doi.org/10.2166/wh.2024.270, CC BY 4.0.

Examples

burigangaamr_antibiotics
#> # A tibble: 9 × 8
#>   antibiotic_code antibiotic              antibiotic_class disc_content
#>   <chr>           <chr>                   <fct>            <chr>       
#> 1 PIT             Piperacillin-tazobactam Penicillins      100/10 µg   
#> 2 CTX             Cefotaxime              Cephalosporins   30 µg       
#> 3 CPM             Cefepime                Cephalosporins   30 µg       
#> 4 GEN             Gentamicin              Aminoglycosides  10 µg       
#> 5 AK              Amikacin                Aminoglycosides  30 µg       
#> 6 MRP             Meropenem               Carbapenems      10 µg       
#> 7 IPM             Imipenem                Carbapenems      10 µg       
#> 8 TE              Tetracycline            Tetracyclines    30 µg       
#> 9 CIP             Ciprofloxacin           Fluoroquinolones 5 µg        
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: breakpoint_resistant_max <int>,
#> #   breakpoint_intermediate_min <int>, breakpoint_intermediate_max <int>,
#> #   breakpoint_susceptible_min <int>
